name: Iteri / Rocky Peak
confidence_why: The only statement on record, Conrad and Dye 1975, says contrastive word stress was noted in Ama and only "possibly" in Rocky Peak on the strength of survey wordlists, while Laycock 1973, Laycock 1975 and Conrad and Lewis 1988 say nothing about stress, so neither the type nor the placement of Iteri stress can be defended.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Survey-level impression only: word stress may be lexically contrastive in the Rocky Peak lect (as it demonstrably is in the sister language Ama, where minimal pairs differ only in stress position); the authors hedge with 'possibly', give no Rocky Peak or Iteri examples, and do not name Iteri proper at all. No statement of a default stress position exists.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the claim itself is hedged ('possibly') and based on SIL survey wordlists.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level ('word stress'); based on elicited wordlist items (citation forms) from a 1960s-1973 SIL survey; no stress marked in the published Rocky Peak/Iteri wordlists.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog iter1241 subsumes two survey lects that Conrad & Dye 1975 (Figure B, p.8) list as separate languages: 'Rocky Peak' (275+; other names Laro, Iyo, Yinibu; villages Iwau, Agrame, Uwau) and 'Iteri' (90+; other names Asowi, Sorimin; one group between Rocky Peak and Bo). The only stress remark names Rocky Peak ('possibly'), not Iteri proper. No separate glottocode exists for Rocky Peak (ISO 'rok' is not in Glottolog; Ethnologue/Glottolog list Rocky Peak, Yinibu, Iyo, Laro, Alowiemino as alternative names of Iteri [itr]).
